correctness.rationale: Re-audit of the repaired theorem: a nonzero commuting product would have the common image line of the factors, which a square-zero factor kills. Consequently S=sum of images lies in K=intersection of kernels and the admissible intermediate dimensions are exactly dim S<=d<=dim K. Both ranks are at most r, so the asserted index sets cover, including the zero tuple; neither S=V nor K=0 can occur. Each incidence is closed in the product with the projective Grassmannian and locally a product with r irreducible rank-one cones of dimension n-1. At retained indices r>=d, the images can generate U, giving generic fiber dimension zero. In the reducible range r>=n-d also; choose r vector factors spanning U and independently r covector factors spanning (V/U)*. Then S=K=U, excluding every competing index, not just those of maximal dimension. The interval in the reducible range contains the middle dimensions, yielding the total dimension and strict reducibility including n=2r-1. The companion formula follows directly by one subspace Möbius inversion with the image span fixed; its equivalence with the double-flag marginal follows because both partition and count precisely the same ordered tuples. A separate F2 implementation directly multiplied 106 eligible matrices and counted 2836 pairs and 38536 triples, matching the formula; the triple count with every entry nonzero was 30345. These runs corroborate only those finite cases.
residual_risks: Only the reduced geometric variety is classified. The checks do not establish a scheme structure or singularity assertions.

value.rationale: The repaired result provides a full classification of the reduced commuting locus for every arity on the smallest nonzero nilpotent orbit closure. It answers irreducibility and non-equidimensionality, which cannot be inferred from the largest components alone. The (4,3) example already separates the full component list from a unique largest component. This structural result is useful independently of the credited point-count corollary.
